name: Daphne Perez
life: “I still remember a retired colleague winning money off me at dominoes.” Thursday often includes a stop at the steps at Pier Beach, where Daphne watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I dealt the first hand and lost to a woman I used to supervise on night shift.
appearance: Daphne is easy to recognize by short white hair and darker eyebrows and a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Usually dressed in a brown corduroy jacket with a narrow brass watch set a little fast, Daphne folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing when listening.
personality: Daphne is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To let the retired ward worker win or lose fairly.
family: Carlo Ueda is Daphne’s cousin’s child. Daphne is free to hang up first. Carlo makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The margin reader*, Carlo says, “My dad hated the book but loved the notes. I'm recording just the margins for his walks.”
connections: Ines Baines. The retired worker's chosen birthday includes playing cards with the old supervisor.

reactions.response: Daphne finds out where the big balloon can go without crowding anyone else's bed.
